result.title: Intent-Aware Caching for Efficient LLM Serving
result.summary: Modern LLM serving systems use prefix caching to accelerate multi-turn conversational workloads. They cache the key-value states of previous conversation prefixes and reuse them when subsequent requests share the same prefix, to avoid redundant prefill computation and reduce serving latency. However, achieving a high cache hit rate remains challenging because cache reuse depends on whether a conversation continues and how soon the next turn arrives. Our analysis of real workloads shows that user intent is a useful signal for this behavior, as different intents exhibit different continuation probabilities and inter-turn delays. Based on this key insight, we propose Intent-Aware Caching (IAC), an online eviction policy that classifies requests by intent, learns lightweight reuse statistics from recent serving logs and leverages these statistics to guide an oracle-inspired eviction strategy. Extensive evaluation on real workloads (WildChat and ShareChat) shows that IAC reaches a 34.6% cache hit rate. This substantially outperforms both the previous learning-based approach (18.8%) and traditional methods such as least recently used (LRU, 12.2%), while reducing average serving latency by up to 46.1%.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 Intent-Aware Caching：依据用户意图对请求分类，从近期服务日志学习续聊概率与轮次间隔统计，用以指导 KV 前缀缓存的在线淘汰策略，在真实对话负载上提升命中率并降低时延。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按未来复用可能性决定保留哪些缓存状态」的在线淘汰思路，可能为多轮推理中 latent 状态/证据的保留与跨轮复用提供类比线索，但该文仅关注服务端缓存命中与延迟，未涉及推理内容或 latent 语义，需核查其意图信号是否能对应推理状态价值。
